data.title: RBI lets rupee rise to break one-way bets on further depreciation
data.description:
India's central bank is using the return of foreign inflows to break bets on a one-way slide in the rupee, allowing the currency to strengthen rather than buying dollars to rebuild reserves.

The strategy ​could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers and ease foreign investors' ​concerns over currency losses, analysts and two sources familiar with the Reserve Bank of India's thinking said.

Indian equities have drawn a ‌record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November, reversing nearly two years of selling and providing the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves.

Yet, the RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown in reserves from their $785.7 billion peak, following heavy dollar sales in October to defend the rupee as it approached its record low of 96.96 per dollar.

 

The RBI's dollar purchases during the rupee's recovery have been limited despite around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist and senior economist at ANZ Bank, said.

"We think its immediate priority is to put exporter hedging on a sustained footing and ease forward market imbalances (between importer and exporter hedging)," he added.

"That may require further rupee appreciation."

Nim said the rupee would face stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar. The currency traded at 92.62 on Friday.

The RBI is in "no hurry" to rebuild reserves and could allow ‌the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist, one of the sources said, requesting anonymity due to restrictions on speaking to the media.

The strategy is consistent with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's publicly stated view that the rupee was undervalued.

An RBI spokesperson did not respond to an email seeking comment on the currency strategy.

EARLY SIGNS OF RESET

The rupee fell 4.8% in 2025 and another 5.5% in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows amid India's limited exposure to the AI investment boom and steep valuations.

Persistent weakness prompted foreign investors to build short rupee positions in the offshore non-deliverable forwards market, exporters to retain dollar earnings and ​importers to step up hedging.

The resulting spiral prompted the RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions and allow ‌oil companies to buy dollars directly from its reserves.

With the rupee now up more than 4% from its lows, expectations are shifting.

Exporter hedging volumes over the past week were significantly higher than levels seen throughout the year, the head of markets at ​a large private-sector bank ‌said, citing renewed hedging of future dollar receivables by Indian IT companies.

Investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, ‌helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.

FLEXIBILITY ON RATES

A sustained recovery in the rupee would provide the RBI higher flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation conditions, rather than having to ‌contend with ​currency weakness. This, ​in turn, could strengthen the rupee's fundamental support.

"Credible moves" on interest rates to address domestic sources of inflation would do more to ease underlying pressures on the rupee, said Aaron Hurd, senior portfolio manager for currency at State Street ‌Investment Management.

"We need to see ​2-3 more rate hikes over the coming quarters, preferably front-loaded with a hike at each of the next two meetings."

data.title: Axis MF launches Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index Fund: NFO dates, key details
data.description:
Investors looking for exposure to both large-cap and mid-cap stocks through a single passive fund can consider a new offering from Axis Mutual Fund, which has launched the Axis Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index Fund. The new fund offer (NFO) opens on November 27 and will remain open until December 11, 2026.
 
The open-ended index fund will track the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Total Return Index (TRI), subject to tracking error. It will invest in a portfolio designed to mirror the index, which combines large-cap and mid-cap stocks in equal proportions.
 

What are the key features of the Axis Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index Fund?

- NFO period: November 27 to December 11, 2026
 
- Benchmark: Nifty LargeMidcap 250 TRI
- Fund managers: Nandik Mallik and Rohit Gautam
- Minimum investment: ₹100, followed by investments in multiples of ₹1
- Allocation: 50 per cent to large-cap stocks and 50 per cent to mid-cap stocks
- Exit load: 0.25 per cent if redeemed or switched out within 15 days of allotment; nil thereafter
- Riskometer: Very High

What does the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index offer?

 
The Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index comprises 100 companies from the Nifty 100 and 150 companies from the Nifty Midcap 150. Together, these stocks represent approximately 75 per cent of India's listed market capitalisation, according to Axis Mutual Fund.
 
The index maintains a 50:50 allocation between large-cap and mid-cap stocks, with weights reset quarterly to maintain this balance. This means investors get exposure to established businesses as well as mid-sized companies that may be expanding their operations and market presence.
 
The index also has relatively lower concentration in its largest constituents. As of October 30, 2026, its top 10 stocks accounted for around 22 per cent of the index, compared with 43 per cent in the Nifty 100 and 53 per cent in the Nifty 50, according to the fund house.
 

How has the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 Index performed?

 
Over the 10-year period ended October 30, 2026, the Nifty LargeMidcap 250 TRI delivered a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.8 per cent, according to Axis Mutual Fund.
 
In comparison, the Nifty 100 TRI returned 11.7 per cent and the Nifty 50 TRI 11.6 per cent over the same period, the fund house said.
 
Past performance may or may not be sustained in the future and does not indicate the returns investors can expect from the new fund.
 

What should investors consider before investing?

 
The fund follows a passive strategy, meaning it will seek to replicate the index rather than actively select stocks in an attempt to outperform it. Its returns, before expenses, will aim to correspond with those of the benchmark, subject to tracking error.
 
A 50 per cent allocation to mid-caps can expose investors to greater volatility and liquidity risks than a portfolio dominated by large-cap stocks. While the index spreads investments across 250 companies, its returns can still be affected by market downturns, particularly when mid-cap stocks face sharper corrections.
 
Investors should also consider whether they already have exposure to large-cap and mid-cap stocks through other mutual funds. Adding another fund with similar holdings may not necessarily improve portfolio diversification.
 
The scheme and its benchmark are both categorised as Very High risk on the Riskometer, according to the fund house.
 
The fund is intended for investors seeking long-term equity exposure through a passive strategy, but investors should assess their risk tolerance, investment horizon and existing portfolio allocation before investing.

data.title: US could hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site if strikes resume: Trump
data.description:
US President Donald Trump has warned that the United States could target Iran's underground Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility if it launches fresh military strikes, even as he claimed that Washington had victory within reach and was allowing Tehran to reach a deal, ANI reported.
 
Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday (local time), Trump said the US had not detected significant activity at the facility but would strike it if military action resumed.
 
“If we did anything, we would absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain, but we haven't seen any real activity there,” Trump said.
 
Pickaxe Mountain is a heavily fortified underground facility near Iran's Natanz uranium enrichment complex. The site has emerged as a potential target amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.
 
 
Trump's remarks came during a series of Thanksgiving calls with American military personnel, alongside First Lady Melania Trump. During the interaction, he claimed that Iran's military capabilities had been severely weakened and said Washington was still allowing Tehran to negotiate.
 
“We have victory at hand. It will happen whenever I want it to happen. We are trying to be nice. We are giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that,” Trump said.
 
He also claimed that Iran's air force and navy had been wiped out and that Tehran had been unable to resume operations at nuclear facilities previously targeted by the US.
 
Trump further said that Iran had missiles capable of reaching Europe, while reiterating that preventing Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons remained a key US objective.

Iran says diplomacy remains an option

Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said Tehran remained open to diplomacy but was currently prioritising the country's resilience against external pressure and efforts to maintain trade routes.
 
In an interview with state news agency IRNA, Araghchi said Iranian officials, particularly those stationed in neighbouring countries, were working to ensure that the country's requirements were met and trade routes remained operational.
 
“Our main focus is on the country's resilience and helping to increase resilience against the pressures that enemies apply through various means,” he said.
 
Addressing the possibility of negotiations with Washington, Araghchi said diplomacy remained part of Iran's approach, but added that countering sanctions and external pressure was a more immediate priority.
 
“Negotiation is part of our work, and we have not forgotten it, and we are pursuing it; but in the current situation, there is also a more important mission, and that is to discourage the enemies from the sanctions and pressures they are imposing on our country,” he said.
 
Araghchi also confirmed that mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan were continuing, with both countries conveying proposals and suggestions to Tehran.

Iran accuses Israel of pushing for fresh conflict

In a separate interview with Shahrara News, Araghchi accused Israel of making statements intended to create an atmosphere conducive to another conflict and draw Washington into a fresh war with Tehran.
 
He alleged that Israel was making claims about Iran to justify further military action, adding that the country remained prepared to defend itself.
 
Araghchi also claimed that American public opinion was increasingly recognising what he described as the prioritisation of Israeli interests over those of the US.
 
(With inputs from ANI)

data.title: Gold, silver prices extend rebound on strong buying at lower levels
data.description:
Gold and silver prices rose sharply on Friday, November 27, as buying at lower levels and short covering followed a steep recent decline. However, strong US economic data and the Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance kept concerns over further interest-rate increases alive.
 
At the time of writing, gold futures on Comex were trading near $3,630 per ounce, while silver was trading near $43.40 per ounce.
 
In the domestic market, gold futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) were trading near ₹1,23,900 per 10 gram, while silver futures were trading near ₹1,51,400 per kg.

Gold prices rise

Gold futures opened higher. On the MCX, the benchmark December gold contract opened ₹2,028 higher at ₹1,24,300 per 10 gram. The previous close was ₹1,22,272.
 
 
At the time of writing, the contract was trading ₹1,612 higher at ₹1,23,884.
 
Gold futures had touched a high of ₹1,59,700 per 10 gram earlier this year.

Silver jumps above ₹1.5 lakh

Silver futures also opened sharply higher. On the MCX, the benchmark December silver contract opened ₹5,833 higher at ₹1,51,676 per kg. The previous close was ₹1,45,843.
 
At the time of writing, the contract was trading ₹5,551 higher at ₹1,51,394.
 
Silver futures had touched a high of ₹4,20,048 per kg earlier this year.

Gold, silver jump in global market

Gold and silver were trading sharply higher in the international market.
 
On Comex, gold opened at $3,590.30 per ounce. The previous closing price was $3,535.80. At the time of writing, it was trading $96.20 higher at $3,632 per ounce.
 
Gold prices had touched a high of $5,586.20 per ounce earlier this year.
 
Comex silver futures opened at $41.27 per ounce. The previous closing price was $40.05. At the time of writing, silver was trading $3.38 higher at $43.43 per ounce.
 
Silver prices had touched a high of $121.79 per ounce earlier this year.

Is the rebound in gold and silver gathering pace?

Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research at Kotak Neo, said silver was leading the rebound that had been expected after the heavy sell-off in precious metals.
 
Gold had fallen below $3,500 per ounce on Wednesday for the first time since September 2025, but recovered above that level within the same trading session. Before the Indian market opened on Friday, gold had risen to around $3,630 per ounce, a gain of nearly 2 per cent. Silver was up around 5 per cent near $43.70 per ounce.
 
Ajay Kedia, director, Kedia Advisory, said gold and silver had recovered as equity markets stabilised and selling pressure eased.
 
However, expectations of a US Federal Reserve rate increase in December could limit the upside, he said.

Levels to watch

According to Kedia, gold was technically witnessing short covering. Open interest declined 16.4 per cent to 6,517 contracts, while prices rose by ₹1,135.
 
Gold has support at ₹1,21,200, followed by ₹1,20,140.
 
The technical data placed resistance at ₹1,23,610, followed by ₹1,24,960. However, the current gold price quoted in the report, at ₹1,23,884, has already crossed the first resistance level, bringing the next level into focus.
 
Silver was also witnessing short covering. Open interest declined 5.29 per cent to 9,056 contracts, while prices rose by ₹3,326.
 
Silver has support at ₹1,44,470, followed by ₹1,43,100.
 
The technical data placed resistance at ₹1,48,010, followed by ₹1,50,170. However, the current silver price quoted in the report, at ₹1,51,394, has already crossed both resistance levels.

MCX, Comex prices

  
Note: MCX gold futures prices are in rupees per 10 gram, while MCX silver futures prices are in rupees per kg. Comex gold and silver futures prices are in dollars per ounce. Last traded prices are as of the time of writing.

data.title: Supriya Lifescience shares soar 9% as firm to mull first-ever buyback
data.description:
Supriya Lifescience share buyback: Shares of pharma company Supriya Lifescience gained nearly 9 per cent in Friday's trading session after the company set a board meeting date to consider its first-ever buyback.
 
The company yesterday informed exchanges that a board meeting is scheduled to be held on Wednesday, December 2, 2026, inter alia, to consider and approve the proposal for buyback of the equity shares of the company, subject to necessary approvals.
 
Following the announcement, Supriya Lifescience's share price hit the day's high of ₹660.15 on the BSE, up 8.96 per cent from the last closing price of ₹605.85.
 
Virat Jagad, senior technical research analyst at Bonanza, said that the technical view is bearish as the stock trades below the 20, 50, 100, and 200 EMAs.
 
 
"RSI stands at 38.70, reflecting weak momentum near lower levels. Price action shows a breakdown below recent consolidation toward the 600–615 zone after failing to hold above 760–770. We suggest avoiding fresh entries at current levels and awaiting a decisive breakout above 775," he added. CHECK Stock Market LIVE Updates

Supriya Lifescience Q2 results

In the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27), Supriya Lifescience posted a 42 per cent year-on-year (YoY) decline in the net profit to ₹29.25 crore. The company had posted a profit of ₹50.43 crore in the same period last year.
 
Meanwhile, it recorded revenue from operations of ₹206.30 crore, up 3.2 per cent YoY from ₹199.83 crore in Q2 FY26.
 
EBITDA for Q2 FY27 stood at ₹45.40 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 22.0 per cent, compared to ₹72.65 crore and a margin of 36.4 per cent in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
 
The operating performance was impacted by three factors: Firstly, the regulatory changes in the LATAM market affected demand for some of its higher-margin products. Secondly, it incurred higher operating expenses at our Ambernath facility, which is currently in the ramp-up phase. Thirdly, due to the ongoing war and geopolitical tensions, raw material and solvent prices remained high which also impacted margins during the quarter.
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: 9.25 lakh Indians became OECD citizens in five years, up 40%: Report
data.description:
Around 925,000 Indian citizens acquired the nationality of a member country of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) between 2020 and 2024, a 40 per cent increase from the previous five-year period, according to the OECD's International Migration Outlook 2026, released earlier this month.
 
India remained the largest country of former nationality among people acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries during the period, ahead of Mexico and Syria, whose nationals accounted for 590,248 and 588,219 citizenship acquisitions, respectively.
 
The number of Indians acquiring citizenship rose from 654,821 during 2015-2019 to 925,000 in 2020-2024. Among other major source countries, acquisitions by Syrian nationals surged nearly five-fold, while those by Chinese nationals declined by 11.9 per cent to 342,808.
  
Acquisitions of citizenship in OECD countries by former nationality (2020–24 vs 2015–19):
 
India: 925,737 (up 41.4 per cent from 654,821)
Mexico: 590,248 (down 3.1 per cent from 609,115)
Syria: 588,219 (up 497.4 per cent from 98,463)
Morocco: 507,951 (up 19.6 per cent from 424,538)
Philippines: 503,679 (up 16.2 per cent from 433,602)
China: 342,808 (down 11.9 per cent from 389,316)
 
The OECD has 38 member countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Japan and several European nations.
 

Canada accounts for largest share of Indian citizenship acquisitions

 
Country-specific data show that 230,337 Indians acquired citizenship in OECD member countries in 2024, compared with 224,630 in 2023. Canada accounted for the largest share, with 87,320 Indians becoming citizens in 2024, followed by the US (48,820) and Australia (28,969).
 
The trend was similar in 2023, when Canada granted citizenship to 78,487 Indians, followed by the US (52,360) and Australia (40,361).
 
Canada has been a major contributor to the rise in Indian citizenship acquisitions. Around 261,000 Indians became Canadian citizens between 2020 and 2024, a 150 per cent increase from the preceding five-year period. The US, the UK and Australia also recorded high numbers.
 
The figures point to the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While migration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions indicate how many immigrants have taken the additional step of becoming nationals of their destination country. 
ALSO READ: US student visa rule struck down: Relief for Indians, but what next?
 

Indian migration to OECD countries slows

 
Despite the rise in citizenship acquisitions, the pace of Indian migration to OECD member countries slowed in 2024. India remained the largest country of origin for new migrants to the bloc, but the number fell 19 per cent to 494,000 in 2024 from 607,000 in 2023.
 
The OECD report also found that around 3 million people acquired the nationality of an OECD member country in 2025. The US accounted for nearly 900,000 new citizens, an increase of 9 per cent over 2024. Germany and Spain recorded around 300,000 each, with increases of 9 per cent and 6 per cent, respectively.
 
Canada ranked fourth, with nearly 300,000 new citizens, following a 22 per cent decline from the previous year.
 
“Migration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16 per cent of employment across the OECD,” OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann said.
 
With ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring, he said, calling for better access to jobs, finance, business networks and support for immigrant entrepreneurs.
 
Immigrants accounted for 12 per cent of the population across OECD member countries in 2025, compared with 9 per cent in 2015. In more than half of the member countries, immigrants contributed at least 50 per cent of employment growth between 2014 and 2024.
 

Leading OECD countries granting citizenship to Indians:

 
2024:
 
Canada: 87,320
United States: 48,820
Australia: 28,969
United Kingdom: 24,888
New Zealand: 5,778
Total across OECD countries: 230,337
 
2023:
 
Canada: 78,487
United States: 52,360
Australia: 40,361
United Kingdom: 18,319
New Zealand: 6,609
Total across OECD countries: 224,630
 

Indian students remain among largest groups overseas

 
ALSO READ: Canada could admit 662k permanent residents in 2027, 74% above target: RBC
 
India also continued to be a major source of international students in OECD countries, although overall student inflows declined. The number of international students entering OECD member countries fell from 1.9 million in 2024 to 1.6 million in 2025, with much of the decline concentrated in traditional English-speaking destinations.
 
European countries, particularly Austria, Germany and Italy, continued to attract more international students. China and India remained the two largest source countries. The gap between them narrowed, with 829,000 Indian students and 850,000 Chinese students enrolled across OECD member countries.
 
The report also found that one in five STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) graduates across OECD countries was foreign-born. Immigrants were also over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative businesses. However, many continued to work in lower-productivity firms and sectors, with their skills not being fully utilised.
 
Permanent migration to OECD member countries declined by 1.6 per cent in 2025, falling for the second consecutive year. However, it remained historically high at nearly 6 million new permanent immigrants. The category covers people moving for family reunification, employment or humanitarian reasons with long-term rights to stay.
 
With countries such as the US, the UK, Canada and Australia tightening immigration policies, the decline in temporary worker and student arrivals could continue over the coming years. However, the latest citizenship figures show that Indians continue to account for the largest number of new citizens across OECD member countries.
 

Annual number of Indians acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries:

 
2010: 133,280
2011: 113,640
2012: 105,067
2013: 134,364
2014: 129,190
2015: 127,374
2016: 129,323
2017: 121,151
2018: 121,299
2019: 155,674
2020: 132,621
2021: 132,877
2022: 205,272
2023: 224,630
2024: 230,337

data.title: UGC NET December 2026: NTA opens exam city change facility, check process
data.description:
The National Testing Agency (NTA) has provided an option for candidates taking the UGC NET December 2026 exam to modify their assigned exam city. As stated in the announcement, this opportunity will be accessible until November 29, 2026, at 11:55 pm. Candidates must complete the procedure before the cutoff. 
 
The new exam city will be assigned based on seat availability. The NTA also mentioned that allocation will be on a first-come, first-served basis. Candidates need to thoroughly check their choice before requesting, as the decision will be final and cannot be altered after submission.

UGC NET December 2026: How to select a different exam city?

UGC-NET December 2026: Exam City Change Opportunity Candidates who have been allotted an Examination City outside their four preferred choices can now select another available Examination City. How to Choose: Visit https://t.co/Y7NeernoHZ Log in using your Application Number and Password/Date of Birth. Select another Examination City from the available options. Important Dates & Instructions: Last Date: 29 November 2026 (11:55 PM) Selection is subject to seat availability. Allotment will be on a first-come, first-served basis. Once submitted, the choice will be final and cannot be changed. Helpdesk: ugcnet@nta.ac.in | 011-40759000 / 1800-180-4747 UGC-NET दिसंबर 2026: परीक्षा शहर (Exam City) बदलने का अवसर जिन उम्मीदवारों को उनकी चार पसंदीदा विकल्पों (preferred choices) के बाहर कोई परीक्षा शहर आवंटित किया गया है, वे अब उपलब्ध विकल्पों में से दूसरा परीक्षा शहर चुन सकते हैं। कैसे चुनें: आधिकारिक वेबसाइट https://t.co/Y7NeernoHZ पर जाएं। अपने एप्लिकेशन नंबर (Application Number) और पासवर्ड/जन्मतिथि (Password/Date of Birth) से लॉग इन करें। उपलब्ध विकल्पों में से दूसरा परीक्षा शहर चुनें। महत्वपूर्ण तिथियां और निर्देश: अंतिम तिथि: 29 नवंबर 2026 (रात 11:55 बजे तक) शहर का चयन सीटों की उपलब्धता के अधीन होगा। आवंटन 'पहले आओ, पहले पाओ' (first-come, first-served) के आधार पर किया जाएगा। एक बार सबमिट करने के बाद, चुना गया विकल्प अंतिम होगा और उसमें कोई बदलाव नहीं किया जा सकेगा। सहायता केंद्र: ugcnet@nta.ac.in | 011-40759000 / 1800-180-4747 #UGCNET #UGCNETDec2026 #NTA #UGC #ExamUpdate

— National Testing Agency (@NTA_Exams) November 26, 2026
Visit the official website of UGC NET at ugcnet.nta.nic.in.
 
 
Click on Login
 
Fill in the application number and Password/ Date of Birth 
 
The option will display only for eligible candidates. 
 
The list shows only cities where capacity is currently available. Choose the city.
 
Save and submit the document. 
ALSO READ: UPPSC PCS admit card 2026: How to download hall ticket PDF for prelims

UGC NET December 2026 Helpdesk

For errors or assistance related to the examination city change facility, candidates can contact the NTA through the below channels:
 
Email: ugcnet@nta.ac.in
 
Helpline: 011-40759000
 
Toll-free number: 1800-180-4747. 

About UGC NET December 2026

According to the details provided, of the 9,76,008 candidates assigned examination cities, 8,74,121 candidates (89.56%) were allotted their first preferred city, 9,53,958 candidates (97.74%) were allotted a city from among their 4 preferred cities; and 22,050 candidates (2.26%) were allotted a location outside their 4 preferred cities. 
 
NTA has decided to let these 22,050 candidates pick another Examination City from the cities where capacity is available. 

All about UGC NET December 2026 exam city choice

In certain cities, a higher number of applicants sought positions than there were computer-based testing seats. When a candidate’s 4 chosen cities lacked any open seats, they were assigned to the closest city that had available slots, determined by the address listed on their application. 
 
This process was implemented to ensure every applicant secures a testing seat according to the planned timeline. However, the NTA has introduced a service allowing candidates to select an exam city that still has openings. These decisions might offer greater convenience for candidates than the city currently assigned to them.  
ALSO READ: NTA UGC NET December 2026 schedule out, check subject-wise exam dates

More about the UGC NET December Exam 2026 

A decision, once made cannot be changed. It should be understood that the number of seats available in each city is restricted and will be assigned according to the order of applications received. 
 
Participants who fail to select an alternative city by the specified deadline will retain the Examination City indicated on their Advance City Intimation Slip. The UGC-NET December 2026 Admit Card will be made available on the official website on December 7, 2026. The Examination City, Centre, Date, and Shift listed on the Admit Card will be final.

data.title: Defence index surges 3%; BEML, Data Patterns, Solar, Paras soar up to 11%
data.description:
Defence shares price movement

 
Shares of defence companies, both public and private, were in demand, with the Nifty India Defence index surging 3.3 per cent to 9,248.10 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Friday’s intraday deals backed by a strong rally in BEML, Data Patterns India, Solar Industries and Paras Defence.
 
At 10:25 AM, the Nifty India Defence index was up 2.94 per cent at 9,216.30, compared to a 0.11 per cent decline in the Nifty 50.
 
Among individual stocks, BEML soared 11 per cent, while Ideaforge Technology surged 7 per cent in intraday deals. Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing, Data Patterns India, Solar Industries, Paras Defence and Space Technologies and Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers rallied 6 per cent each. Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Bharat Dynamics (BDL), Centum Electronics, Dynamatic Technologies and Hindustan Aeronautics were up in the range of 4-5 per cent.
 
 

What’s driving defence stocks?

 
In the past three trading days, the Nifty India Defence index outperformed the market by soaring 5 per cent against a 2 per cent rise in the Nifty 50. However, in the past three months, the defence index underperformed by falling 5.6 per cent compared to a 7 per cent rally in the benchmark index.
 
Analysts at Choice Institutional Equities believe the July to September 2026 quarter (Q2FY27) marks a broadening of revenue growth across the defence sector, but not yet a corresponding improvement in earnings quality. While private players demonstrated a sharper recovery in profitability, defence public sector undertakings (DPSUs) continued to face margin pressure despite healthy revenue growth. 
 
“This divergence reinforces our view that the next phase of sector performance will be driven less by orderbook visibility alone and more by execution efficiency, margin sustainability and conversion of large programmes into profitable revenues,” the brokerage firm said in its defence & aerospace sector Q2FY27 result review. Analysts remain positive on the sector's structural growth opportunity, supported by a rising domestic defence production, indigenisation and exports.
 
“Order books across our defence coverage universe remain on a firm growth trajectory, underscoring strong demand visibility and sustained procurement momentum. Public sector undertakings continue to anchor large, multi-year contracts backed by government spending, while private players are steadily capturing market share through faster execution cycles and a sharper focus on high-value, technology-driven solutions,” the brokerage firm said.
 Analysts forecast that, based on a consistent book-to-bill assumption aligned with historical trends and management commentary, the sector reflects a healthy order pipeline supported by rising defence budgets, policy tailwinds and the government’s strategic push for indigenisation. This combination positions the sector for a structurally robust growth cycle over the medium term, it added.  
Meanwhile, Solar Industries, through its subsidiary Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL), has completed in-house development trials of Bhargavastra, an indigenously developed two-layer Vehicle-Mounted Counter Swarm Drone System. The system combines a 64-tube air defence rocket launcher (Version-I) with a 64-micro-missile launcher (Version-II), featuring autonomous guidance and infrared seekers for engaging multiple drones.
 
The successful development trials mark a key milestone for SDAL in expanding its counter-drone and air-defence portfolio, particularly amid the growing requirement for indigenous systems capable of addressing swarm-drone threats. The development of Version-II with IR-guided micro-missiles, over and above the original rocket-based requirement, enhances the system's engagement capabilities and strengthens SDAL's in-house technology portfolio, ICICI Securities said in a note.
 
The project is linked to the Ministry of Defence’s (MoD's) Jul-24 Project Sanction Order, which envisages one prototype set and 12 deliverable sets following successful prototype demonstration. Progression through prototype demonstration, further trials and subsequent procurement will remain key monitorables for commercial order conversion, the brokerage firm said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. data.title: CERT-In flags security vulnerabilities in WhatsApp, ASUS software: Details
data.description:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has flagged multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business, warning that attackers could exploit the flaws to execute malicious code, access sensitive information and bypass security restrictions on affected devices.
 
In a separate advisory, the cybersecurity agency also identified critical vulnerabilities in software from ASUS, including its Control Center products and Armoury Crate. The ASUS flaws could allow attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrative privileges on affected systems.

WhatsApp vulnerabilities could expose user data

In its advisory CIVN-2026-0576, CERT-In identified multiple vulnerabilities affecting WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business across Android, iOS, Mac desktop and Windows platforms.
 
ALSO READ: WhatsApp partners with Jio, Verizon, more to bring travel eSIM data plans
According to the agency, the vulnerabilities arise from attachment spoofing, SQL injection, improper certificate chain validation, incomplete validation of AI rich response messages and external ad-reply URLs.
 
A remote attacker could exploit these weaknesses by sending a specially crafted message, attachment or URL to a targeted device. Successful exploitation could allow arbitrary code execution, disclosure of sensitive information, bypassing of security restrictions or manipulation of application data.
 
The affected software versions include:
  • WhatsApp for Android: Versions prior to 2.26.35.74 and 2.26.17.4.
  • WhatsApp Business for Android: Versions prior to 2.26.23.70 and 2.26.17.4.
  • WhatsApp for iOS: Versions prior to 2.26.24.72 and 2.26.15.72.
  • WhatsApp Business for iOS: Versions prior to 2.26.23.72.
  • WhatsApp for Mac desktop: Versions prior to 2.26.23.72.
  • WhatsApp for Windows: Versions prior to 2.3000.1032164386.258709.
CERT-In has advised users to apply the relevant updates released by WhatsApp.

CERT-In flags critical vulnerabilities in ASUS software

In a separate advisory, CIVN-2026-0575, CERT-In flagged multiple vulnerabilities in ASUS software, assigning them a critical severity rating.
 
The affected products include ASUS Control Center Express, Control Center Datacenter, Control Center Enterprise and Armoury Crate. The vulnerabilities could allow remote attackers to bypass authentication, forge authentication tokens, obtain administrative control and gain elevated privileges on affected systems.
ALSO READ: WhatsApp rolls out scheduled messages: How to use it and what to know
CERT-In attributed the flaws to hard-coded cryptographic keys, incorrect or missing authorisation checks, and an untrusted search path.
 
An attacker could exploit these weaknesses to create unauthorised administrator accounts, change existing administrator passwords, bypass authentication or execute malicious libraries with elevated privileges. The agency warned that successful exploitation could compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of managed systems.
 
The affected versions are:
  • ASUS Control Center Express: Versions prior to 1.7.29.
  • ASUS Control Center Datacenter: Version 4.0.0.2 and earlier.
  • ASUS Control Center Enterprise: Version 3.1.0.8 and earlier.
  • ASUS Armoury Crate: Versions up to and including 6.7.2.
CERT-In has asked users and organisations running the affected software to install the security updates listed in ASUS's official security advisories.

What users should do

WhatsApp users should check whether their applications are running affected versions and install the latest updates available through the relevant app stores or official channels.
 
Organisations using ASUS Control Center products should prioritise updating their management software, given the possibility of unauthorised administrative access and privilege escalation. Individual users should also ensure that Armoury Crate is updated beyond the affected versions.
